gre-vocab-defmatch.title: GRE Vocabulary
gre-vocab-defmatch.description: Which word means: "To give a false impression of; to contradict or misrepresent."?
gre-vocab-defmatch.explanation: belie (verb): To give a false impression of; to contradict the appearance of. A calm surface can belie a turbulent interior. Do not confuse with 'lie around' — that is an archaic sense not tested on the GRE. Corroborate (to confirm) is a useful contrast: corroborate means to back up a claim; belie means to undercut one.
gre-vocab-defmatch.source: Wiktionary (via dictionaryapi.dev) — word selection from public GRE frequency lists

gre-vocab-defmatch.title: GRE Vocabulary
gre-vocab-defmatch.description: Which word means: "To tolerate or endure (typically used in the negative: 'would brook no interruption')."?
gre-vocab-defmatch.explanation: brook (verb): To tolerate or endure — almost always used in the negative. 'She would brook no delay' means she refused to accept any delay at all. Assuage (to relieve) and condone (to overlook) are plausible traps: assuage softens something; condone accepts it passively; brook specifically means to put up with, and the negative construction is what the GRE tests.
gre-vocab-defmatch.source: Wiktionary (via dictionaryapi.dev) — word selection from public GRE frequency lists
